lines: Clean wool feels ordinary until winter reminds you it is not.
A spilled dye pot once made half the village look <gradient:#55ff55:#ff55ff>festive</gradient> by mistake.
One late evening, the whole loom jammed because I trusted a knot.
There is a story from the loom, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Most stories here begin with someone saying, 'It will only take a moment.' They are always wrong.
I remember the smell of rain, the sound of the bell, and everyone suddenly pretending they had a plan.
The funny part came later. At the time, nobody was laughing.
A village story changes depending on who got embarrassed in it.
I could make it grand, but honestly, it was mostly mud, noise, and bad timing.
Still, we tell it because we made it through, and that makes people stand a little straighter.
Once a sheep got onto a roof and refused to explain its method.
A lamb followed me into the square and became the day's main news.
I dyed wool the wrong color once and the village called it fashion to be polite.
During a storm, the flock packed together like they had invented courage.
A child counted sheep aloud and fell asleep before the sheep did.
The old ram once stared down a trader and won a discount by accident.
I found a lost bell in a wool sack after searching everywhere sensible.
One winter a single blanket got passed around more than gossip.
A sheep ate part of a map and made travel more adventurous.
I once sheared in a hurry and created a very uneven legend.
The loom broke on a festival morning and everyone suddenly cared about knots.
A lamb learned to open a gate and I learned to distrust innocence.
There was a fog so thick the flock sounded closer than my own hands.
I mended a cloak after a raid and found ash woven into the seam.
The flock once moved as one for ten steps. We still speak of it with awe.
